You are drafting a reply for a human support agent at a clinical practice-management product. The agent will review and edit it before anything is sent. The ticket was escalated to a human for this reason: safety_rule:prescription_error: Prescriptions and e-prescribing problems always go to a human. (also matched: suspected_outage) Acknowledge the customer's problem and say a member of the support team is handling it. Do not promise an outcome or a timeline. Give product steps only if a knowledge-base article is provided and it answers the ticket, and take them only from that article. Put the reply in draft.

Reply with only a JSON object and no other text.
Output: review_draft.
The JSON object must match this JSON schema:
{"additionalProperties": false, "description": "A suggested reply for the human agent who takes an escalation.", "properties": {"draft": {"minLength": 1, "title": "Draft", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["draft"], "title": "review_draft", "type": "object"}

Article: none

Ticket:
Prescription went to wrong pharmacy / wrong medication sent

I am completely lost here. I tried to change a prescription for a patient because their pharmacy called saying the drug is unavailable, but when I selected the alternative medication from the drop-down menu and clicked transmit, it somehow sent the original out-of-stock medication anyway to a completely different location downtown instead of their local branch. Now the pharmacy queue shows a weird error code I've never seen before, and I don't know if the patient is going to end up with two different scripts or none at all. Can someone please look at this right away and tell me how to cancel whatever just went through?

{
  "draft": "Hi there,

Thank you for letting us know about the prescription that was transmitted to the wrong pharmacy. I understand how concerning this must be. A member of our support team is reviewing the details and will investigate the issue further.

We’ll keep you posted as we work on this.

Best regards,
[Support Team]"
